title: Communicate & find your way
short: Family contact, emergency radio, ham radio, map and compass
intro: Ways to reach family and get official warnings when phones and internet are down or overloaded, what you need to know before using two-way radios, and how to find your way with a map and compass or signal for help.

limits.text: Ham radio operators must pass a test and obtain an FCC license (Technician, General or Extra).
You need an FCC license to communicate on ham radio (the article says the test can be prepared for in days).
FRS radios may be used without a license, but transmitting on GMRS radios requires a license.
FCC rules allow an amateur station in distress to use any means at its disposal to attract attention and get help (the rule as printed in the ARES manual).
NOAA Weather Radio usually reaches about 40 miles; buildings and valleys can block it, so test a receiver where you will use it.
A compass points to magnetic north, not true north; the difference varies by place and changes over time.
If trapped, shout only as a last resort — it can make you inhale dangerous dust; tap on a pipe or wall or use a whistle.
